after: Project Delivery Report
This report sets out the delivery approach, the review points, and the decisions needed to keep the project moving on a predictable schedule.
The plan uses a practical monthly cadence so the team can make decisions with current information and resolve issues before they affect delivery.
The sections that follow describe the working plan, the delivery measures, and the governance routine for the project.
Project Scope

The project will deliver a defined first release with documented requirements, tested workflows, and a concise handoff package. The work focuses on the activities required to move from an agreed scope to a usable release.
The delivery team will maintain a single record of decisions and open questions. This record will help the team distinguish approved work from items that need further review.
The first release will be judged against clear acceptance criteria. Changes that affect timing, cost, or the intended outcome will be reviewed before work begins.
Delivery checkpoints
Checkpoint
Purpose
Expected result
Scope review
Confirm required work
Approved requirements
Build review
Assess completed work
Testable release candidate
Launch review
Confirm readiness
Handoff decision
Delivery Measures
The team will review progress against the agreed milestones each week. The review will focus on completed work, unresolved dependencies, and the next set of decisions needed from project sponsors.
A short status update will record schedule changes, material risks, and actions that require an owner. This keeps the plan usable without creating a separate reporting process.
The following actions support a consistent delivery rhythm.
Review open dependencies before each milestone
Record decisions and assigned actions
Share test results with the release group
The delivery measures should be reviewed at the same time as the working plan. If a milestone changes, the team should update the related actions and record the reason for the change.
Governance and Review
Project governance will use brief decision meetings at the points where scope, timing, or release readiness may change. The meetings will focus on the information required for the next decision.

The project lead will maintain the decision record and will bring unresolved issues to the appropriate sponsor. Sponsors will review material changes promptly so the team can continue work with a clear direction.
At the end of the release, the team will compare completed work with the acceptance criteria and identify any follow-up items for the next planning cycle.
Next Steps
The project lead will confirm the next review date and share the current decision record with the delivery team.
Each owner will update assigned actions before the review so that unresolved work and timing changes are visible.
The team will use the review outcome to confirm the work planned for the next delivery period.
